reanchor_receipts.content:
## Findings ledger
- [C1.DOC3.F1] The source documents capitalism as a social-historical regime and conceptual object, not a single country or empirical jurisdiction; its defining object is the social institution that makes the economy central and treats economic criteria as the supreme value of social life — dim: case_identity — anchor: "the characteristic trait of capitalism, among all the forms of social-historical life, is obviously the positing of the economy—of production and consumption" — doc: castoriadis1997_rationality_of_capitalism — case: capitalism as a social-historical regime — object-time-scope: comparative historical and conceptual treatment of capitalism across social-historical forms; no single bounded jurisdiction — criterion: what institution or approach is being compared, and what distinguishes it — confidence: high
- [C1.DOC3.F3] The source distinguishes a classical phase of capitalism lasting until around 1975 from a present phase beginning approximately in the early 1970s, marked by globalization and deregulated international capital flows — dim: case_identity — anchor: "In the present phase of capitalism, that is, since approximately the early 1970s, all the foregoing remains true" — doc: castoriadis1997_rationality_of_capitalism — case: capitalism across historical phases — object-time-scope: classical phase until around 1975 and present phase since approximately the early 1970s, with discussion extending to 1996–1997 — criterion: how do comparable cases or phases differ by period and institutional configuration — confidence: high
- [C1.DOC3.F4] The source treats global capitalism as an expanded contemporary object whose production and capital flows operate across previously industrialized and “emergent” countries, while stressing that their production conditions are not homogeneous — dim: case_identity — anchor: "the effective globalization of capitalist production—which is made possible by new developments both technological" — doc: castoriadis1997_rationality_of_capitalism — case: contemporary global capitalism — object-time-scope: global production and international capital flows in the phase since approximately the early 1970s, discussed from the standpoint of 1997 — criterion: what is the territorial scale and degree of comparability across the cases or settings — confidence: high

reanchor_receipts.content:
## Findings ledger
- [C3.DOC2.F2] Tocqueville's account is historically and institutionally non-equivalent to contemporary democracy because it described a disappearing Jeffersonian social situation rather than merely a constitutional arrangement — dim: comparison_limits — case: Tocqueville's United States — criterion: Does a historical description of social conditions answer a contemporary question about political power? — limit: context — pattern-tested: Tocqueville's account directly represents contemporary democracy — anchor: "Tocqueville was in the United States at the beginning of the 1830s, but the United States he was describing already no longer existed when he was there." — doc: castoriadis1990_what_democracy — confidence: high
- [C3.DOC2.F4] The text identifies national sovereignty and national social formations as limits on universal comparison, since universal democratic principles encounter different national contexts and political histories — dim: comparison_limits — case: national polities — criterion: Can universal democratic principles be applied without accounting for national institutional and historical differences? — limit: context — pattern-tested: democracy has a single universally transferable political meaning — anchor: "they never deal with anyone besides men in general." — doc: castoriadis1990_what_democracy — confidence: high
- [C3.DOC2.F5] The text rejects treating Western-style democracy as universally generalizable because its material and ecological conditions are sharply unequal across the global population — dim: comparison_limits — case: rich and poor regions — criterion: Can a democratic regime be generalized across cases without comparing material and ecological conditions? — limit: comparability — pattern-tested: Western-style democracy can be universalized without changing its socioeconomic basis — anchor: "In the other regions, with their population of 4. billion persons, the GNP does not exceed, on average, fiveor six-hundred dollars." — doc: castoriadis1990_what_democracy — confidence: high
